newsitem.title: USA: British groups back lead regulator, say US unsure.
newsitem.headline: British groups back lead regulator, say US unsure.

text.p: Britain is keen to press ahead with plans to develop a "lead regulator" to handle international financial crises but U.S. watchdogs were only lukewarm on the idea, a U.K. regulator said on Thursday.

Nicholas Durlacher, chairman of Britain's Securities and Futures Authority (SFA), said at a derivatives conference here the SFA was a fervent supporter of the concept, recently discussed by officials at the Group of Seven meeting in Berlin in February.

"What we have assessed from Barings and BCCI is you really need someone who can sit on top of the heap and look at the consequences of a multinational operation," Durlacher said in an interview with Reuters.
He said the need for a lead regulator has increased sharply as companies become more international and carry out sophisticated trading strategies on exchanges around the world.
The collapse of British investment bank Barings Plc in February 1995 after a trader carried out unauthorised deals on exchanges in Asia was a case in point, he said.
A lead regulator might be a central bank or a national regulator in a company's country of origin, Durlacher said.
